public_rationale: The forecast has no deadline. No searched record establishes a lasting end to the relevant doubling process. METR's decision to stop updating its chart is a reporting change, not evidence that capabilities stopped improving. Continued gains through the cutoff would likewise not refute a prediction about eventual limits.
limitations: The claim's breadth makes decisive resolution difficult.
Any numerical rule for a sustained slowdown would add a threshold Marcus did not supply.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI progress will not keep doubling indefinitely.

statement.excerpt: Babies don’t keep doubling forever, and nor will AI progress.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that exponential improvement in AI capability eventually ends or changes, not that progress immediately stops.
The surrounding discussion makes METR task horizons a relevant indicator, but does not make them an exhaustive measure of AI progress.
A temporary slowdown, benchmark saturation, or interruption in reporting does not establish a lasting end to capability growth.
criteria.support_condition: A decisive, documented ceiling or lasting structural break establishes that the capability-doubling process under discussion cannot continue indefinitely.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Indefinitely continued doubling would contradict the literal claim. No finite sequence of continued gains alone can demonstrate that outcome.
